Samir — thanks for sending the sample and for the clear goals. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed next steps: 

Recap:
- Primary use: developer docs + API example search (short queries, long docs).
- Metrics you care about: recall@10, MRR, and stability across weekly ingestion/drift.
- Constraints: GDPR for EU customers (you mentioned EU subset), latency target ~ <60ms p95 for embedding lookups, and cost sensitivity on production usage.

Recommended first-pass models to evaluate:
- redwood-embed-2-small (256-d): low-cost baseline, good for tight latency budgets.
- redwood-embed-4 (768-d): expected solid semantic fidelity for mixed short/long text.
- redwood-embed-4-quant (768-d, int8): lower cost, slight fidelity tradeoff — good candidate for bulk indexing.

Evaluation checklist (we'll run these during the POC):
1) Offline holdout eval: recall@10, recall@100, MRR on your labeled queries.
2) Semantic clustering diagnostics: average cosine similarities within vs between categories; silhouette scores.
3) Dimensionality sanity: compare top-20 PCA explained variance for 256 vs 768 dims to detect over/under-embedding.
4) Drift baseline: weekly KS test on cosine distribution and proportion of queries with similarity < 0.2.
5) Latency & cost: per-100k token embed cost estimate + p95 end-to-end lookup.

Files & links:
- We'll upload a short evaluation plan and a shared Drive folder with benchmarks (link below).
- Please confirm you can share the full 100k sample once we sign the DPA; for initial tests the 5k is fine.

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi to run initial embedding sweep (3 models above) on the 5k sample and return a short bench report (estimated 48 hours).
- Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive (Marissa to lead) to go through the evaluation output and discuss indexing strategies.
- If POC looks good, we’ll propose a minimal Dedicated configuration for production indexing.

If that works I’ll kick off the eval tomorrow and share the first report. Two quick asks from your side: 1) confirm region for data residency (US or EU), 2) sign the quick DPA link so we can ingest the larger sample.

Thanks —

Thanks, Neha — this is great. A couple of clarifying points before you start the sweep: 

- Drift: our content pipeline ingests ~10k new docs per week; we need an early-warning signal for semantic drift that can be reviewed by our ML engineer. 
- Dimensionality question: historically we’ve used 512-d vectors; if the 768-d model yields marginal gains but doubles index size, we'll need to justify cost. Do you have a quick heuristic for expected recall lift per +256 dims?
- Latency: our front-end SLA needs sub-50ms p95 for the final lookup (we can cache heavy queries). Can you include a rough p99 estimate for 100k QPS if we go vector-shard + FAISS HNSW on 1 dedicated pool?

Also — can you share a short example of the prompt sets you run for negative sampling / hard-negative mining for the semantic eval? That helped us previously.

Happy to sign the DPA; I’ll ping legal today. Schedule-wise, Thurs morning PST works for the deep-dive.

—Samir
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Samir — quick technical follow-up from our side before the sweep: 

1) Dimensionality heuristic: empirical rule we use — going from 512->768 typically yields diminishing returns but in mixed-length corpora (short queries + long docs) we often see ~3–6% absolute recall@10 uplift on domain-specific corpora. We’ll quantify this on your 5k sample; if uplift <2%, we recommend 256/512 path for cost reasons.

2) Drift monitoring: suggested baseline checks we will instrument in Redwood Console: weekly cosine KS test (p-value threshold 0.01), fraction of queries with nearest-neighbor similarity < 0.2, and cluster centroid movement (cosine delta). We’ll provide a small alert playbook when we push to Prod.

3) Latency & architecture notes: with FAISS HNSW and a single dedicated pool (N=4 shards recommended for your dataset size), typical p95 lookup times range 20–70ms depending on N and vector dim. For 100k QPS sustained, we recommend Dedicated with autoscaling and local SSD indices; we’ll provide cost estimates in the bench report. p99 will be higher — expect a 1.8–2.5x multiplier on p95 under burst.

4) Prompt sets / hard negatives: attached is a short example of our negative sampling prompts and the mini-hard-negative mining script we run during eval. Example prompts include: 
- "Given query <Q>, return 3 docs that are semantically similar but have different categories."
- "For doc D, sample 5 near neighbors that are background-similar but label-different."

Deliverables timeline:
- 48h: Rishi returns sem-bench-report.csv with recall@10, MRR, cosine distributions for the 3 models.
- Day 5: full evaluation doc with PCA dimensionality plots and recommended embed for pilot.

I’ve attached the sem-bench-report.csv (first-pass) and a draft eval plan. I’ll add a Thurs 10am PST slot to the calendar (link in drive).
